title: A conformance suite manifest
description: Derived from the 14 manifests that actually ship, not from what a manifest was once imagined to look like. An earlier version of this file listed nine keys, forbade everything else, and had no `security-corpus` in its `kind` enum -- so it would have rejected almost every manifest in this repository. Nothing loaded it, so nobody found out. It is enforced by tools/guard-corpus.mjs now, which is the only reason it can be trusted.

kind.description: `security-corpus` is scored by tools/trust-rubric.mjs and carries extra obligations -- adversarial rows, and a `findings` block once every row agrees.

pins.description: What this suite fixes in place, and why it matters ACROSS a language boundary. A suite whose pins could be stated without mentioning two languages is probably a per-language test.

scope.description: What the suite deliberately does NOT cover. Its absence is why 'this suite exists' gets read as 'this value is covered'.

findings.description: What running it actually established. The trust rubric requires this once no row disagrees, because `agrees: true` speaking for itself is how G-36 survived: three languages agreeing on something wrong.

cause.description: WHOSE gap it is. Required alongside a `partial` status, because `partial` alone flattens a port with no runner, a port that is correct while the reference is ambiguous, and a row a language cannot express into one word -- and read as a scoreboard that reports the ports as behind when the reference is behind its own ports. Enforced by tools/parity-gaps.mjs.

authority.description: WHO DECIDES WHAT IS CORRECT, which is a different question from `reference` (who GENERATES the goldens). For almost every family they are the same: the PHP package defines the behaviour and the ports must agree with it, so a disagreement is a port bug. `external` says the definition lives outside this ecosystem entirely -- a published protocol or spec -- and therefore a disagreement between the PHP package and that definition is a PHP BUG, not a port bug. Defaults to `reference` when absent.

authority_note.description: Required when `authority` is `external`: names the actual authority and where it is watched, so a reader can check it rather than take the claim on trust. Enforced by tools/guard-corpus.mjs rather than by this schema -- the validator here is a deliberate subset of JSON Schema (type, required, properties, additionalProperties, enum, minProperties) and silently ignores if/then, so a conditional expressed here would look enforced and would not be.
